en: Then, regarding the deletion marks resembling *visarga* in the manuscript (*C*):

"The *caitya*, however, through its divisions known as the *kumbha*, the *kanaka*, the heap of grain, and the *latā*, is respectively like the shape of the letter *ṭha*, like a crest (*cūḍikā*), like the egg of a bird, and like a sesame seed. [In Tibetan:

The *kumbha* of the *caitya* is, according to its divisions known as gold, a heap of grain, and a creeper, respectively like the shape of the letter *ṭha*, like a crest, like a bird's egg, and like a sesame seed.

When a square field has been made and divided into twelve parts, the *bimba* (vase) is formed by removing portions from two corners—one part, one and a half parts, and two and a half parts—through the process of division and drawing.
That is to say, having divided the square ground into twelve parts, one removes [portions] from two corners consisting of one and a half and two and a half parts; thus, the circle becomes the vase.

The base is formed by half of the *bimba* [dome] and is provided with a rim (*nemi*); the pedestal (*pīṭha*) is likewise half of the *bimba*. Similarly, the parasol (*chattra*) extends from the top of the *dharmī* [the neck] to the end.

By half of the *bimba* it becomes the tiered molding (*bandha*), and by half of the *bimba* it is the pedestal; likewise, up to the pinnacle and the summit, the parasol is determined according to the proportions of the image.
And that [consists of] one, three, five, and thirteen for the Perfect Buddhas and Vajradharas; nine and seven for the Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas.
At a caitya belonging to those who have not yet abandoned desire, there is only a lotus bud and nothing else.
At a caitya for those who have not yet transcended the realm of passion, there is only a circular lotus and nothing other than that.
Likewise, the installation of the central axis (yaṣṭi) should be performed without distinction from the image (bimba).
Thus, the central axis should be fashioned according to the proportions of the statue.
Furthermore, the throne of the four Buddhas has Vairocana as its principal figure;
it is adorned with the four Buddhas upon the four auspicious [vases] outside the central image.

One should perform the installation of pillars in the corners, adorned with Bodhisattvas and the like. Above the central shaft (yaṣṭi), it should be shaped like an umbrella, known as the "rain-cover" (varṣāsthālaka).
It should be supported by brackets and adorned with Bodhisattvas and so forth. The form of the umbrella is above the life-wood (srog shing), and it is designated as the rain-cover.
It should be adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, bells, and networks of small tinkling bells; above that, a jewel should be fashioned, though some say it should be a lotus bud.
An expert in the ritual procedures should have it made according to the rules and endowed with the proper characteristics.

It is adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, bells, and so forth, as well as with rows of tassels. Upon that, one should place jewels; "the circular lotus is at the end," according to some. One should perform the ritual endowed with the defining characteristics through the successive stages of the procedure.
This is the ritual for the characteristics of a *caitya*.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the characteristics of the stūpa.
